findings_closed.summary: returned RelationDecision captured, its exact identity validated, its exact relation-authorizing authority recorded, and the supplied SOURCE_EQUIVALENCE snapshot cross-bound to it (no A/B split)
identity-owning TEMPORAL_EVIDENCE authority now resolved against the exact compared source universe pair
both adopted explicit-unrestricted representations honored in all three scope helpers; no third token; omission still not unrestricted

RR-03 witness replaced with a same-fixture mechanism break that falsifies only owner satisfaction consultation and reopens the authorization path; RR-04 witness rewritten because its old assertion had come to assert the vulnerability the repair closes

residual_risks_for_rereview: isinstance(resolver, SourceRelationResolver) still accepts subclasses, and F7 now trusts the returned decision's content. A hostile SUBCLASS of the real resolver could still return a fabricated AUTHORIZED RelationDecision. HQ220 raised this as a related boundary weakness; it was not one of the four commissioned findings and was not repaired, so it is flagged rather than silently widened.

The governed-use contract mismatch HQ220 identified is unchanged: F7's governed use is an ExactRef while the adopted source-relation owner keys target_use as a non-empty string, so F7 projects governed_use_id.object_id. That remains an integration/producer occupancy gap, not an F7 defect, and HQ should keep it visible.
IDENTITY_CONTRACT_INSTANCE_MISSING remains an upstream estate-occupancy gap. HQ222 consumes competent owner-backed fixtures; it does not create a real production identity instance.

The RR-03 targeted-break witness requires the new production seam and therefore cannot execute against pre-repair production; its pre-repair discriminating power is carried by the three RR-03B scope witnesses, which do fail pre-repair.
